Source: A 44-year-old man presents to the emergency department with palpitations.
His temperature is 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 120/72 mmHg, pulse is 183/min, respirations are 25/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
An ECG is performed as seen in Figure A.
During the exam, the patient states that he feels lightheaded and appears occasionally somnolent.
Physical exam reveals a somnolent and uncomfortable man.
His pulse is rapid and regular.
He says that he feels lightheaded and can’t walk.
Today, his symptoms have been persistent despite taking his medications.
He also has hypertension but does not take any medications.
He has a history of anxiety managed with fluoxetine and lorazepam.
